title: The Quiet New Friend
summary: A girl named Sara notices a quiet new classmate who always sits alone, and a small act of kindness turns into a lasting friendship.
poll: It is always worth the risk to reach out to someone who seems lonely, even if they might say no.

versions.title: A New Friend
versions.text:
Sara is in Grade 5. A new girl sits in her class. Her name is Lama.

Lama sits alone at lunch. She sits alone at play time too. She does not talk to the other kids.

Sara notices this each day. She feels bad. One day, she walks over. She sits by Lama.

"Hi," she says. "Can I sit here?"

Lama looks up. She does not say much. She has a notebook. It is full of bird drawings.

"I like birds too!" Sara says. She wants to share her own book. It has drawings too.

Lama smiles. They talk about birds. They talk about art.

Now Lama is not alone. She sits with Sara each day. They draw at play time. They are good friends now.

Sara is a student in Grade 5 at a school in Riyadh. This year, a quiet new girl joined her class. Her name was Lama, and she had just moved from another city.

Every day, Lama sat by herself at lunch. She sat alone at play time too, and she did not talk to the other kids. Nobody talked to her either.

Sara noticed this each day. At first she said nothing, but she began to feel sorry for Lama. One day, she chose to be kind. She walked over and sat down beside her.

"Hi, I'm Sara," she said with a small smile. "Can I sit with you?"

Lama looked up slowly. She did not say much at first. In her hands was a notebook, full of careful bird drawings.

"Wow, I love drawing birds too!" Sara said happily. She offered to share her own book, which was also full of drawings.

Lama's face changed, and she finally smiled. The two girls spent play time talking about birds to draw.

After that day, Lama was never alone again. She sat with Sara every day, and they drew together at play time. Slowly, they had become true friends.

Sara is a student in Grade 5 at a school in Riyadh. This year, a quiet new girl joined her class. Her name was Lama. She had just moved from another city, leaving her old friends behind.

Every single day, Lama sat by herself. She sat alone during lunch, and she sat alone during play time as well. She did not talk to the other kids. Nobody talked to her either, as if she were invisible in the busy yard.

Sara noticed this pattern day after day, and it began to bother her. At first she said nothing, but slowly she started to feel sorry for Lama. One afternoon, Sara finally chose to act. She walked over and sat down beside her.

"Hi, I'm Sara," she said with a small, friendly smile. "Can I sit here with you?"

Lama looked up slowly, clearly surprised. She did not say much at first, only a quiet "okay." In her hands was a notebook, filled with careful bird drawings.

"Wow, I love drawing birds too!" Sara said happily, leaning closer to look. She offered to share her own book, which was also full of similar drawings.

Lama's face changed completely, and she finally smiled. The two girls spent the rest of play time talking about their favorite birds to draw.

After that day, Lama was never alone again. She sat with Sara every single day. They drew together at every play time. Slowly but surely, the two girls had become true, close friends.

Sara, however, did notice. Day after day, watching Lama sit by herself began to bother her more and more. At first she said nothing, unsure of what to do, but slowly she started to feel sorry for Lama. One afternoon, Sara finally found the courage to act. She walked over and sat down next to her.

"Hi, I'm Sara," she said, offering a small, friendly smile. "Can I sit here with you?"

Lama looked up slowly, clearly surprised that someone wanted to sit beside her. The first few moments felt a little awkward, and she only managed a quiet "okay." In her hands was a notebook, filled with careful sketches of birds.

"Wow, I love drawing birds too!" Sara said happily, leaning closer for a look. She offered to share her own sketchbook, which was full of similar drawings.

Lama's face changed completely, and she finally smiled for the first time that day. The awkwardness melted away as the two girls spent the rest of play time talking about their favorite birds to sketch.

After that day, Lama was never alone again. She sat with Sara at lunch every day, and the two of them sketched together at every play time. Slowly but surely, a quiet new classmate had become a true, close friend.

versions.title: The Quiet New Friend
versions.text:
Sara was a student in Grade 5 at a school in Riyadh. This year, a quiet new girl named Lama had joined her class, having just moved from another city and left all of her old friends behind.

Every single day, Lama sat by herself. She ate lunch alone, and she spent recess alone too, as though she were invisible in the busy, noisy schoolyard. None of her classmates seemed to notice her, or if they did, nobody made any real effort to include her in their games or conversations.

Sara, however, did notice. Day after day, watching Lama sit by herself began to bother her more and more. At first she said nothing, unsure of exactly what to do, but slowly she started to feel genuinely sorry for the quiet new classmate. One afternoon, Sara finally found the courage to do something kind instead of simply watching from a distance. She walked across the yard and sat down beside her.

"Hi, I'm Sara," she said, offering a small, friendly smile. "Can I sit here with you?"

Lama looked up slowly, clearly surprised that anyone wanted to sit beside her. The first few moments felt somewhat awkward, and she only managed a quiet "okay." In her hands was a notebook, filled with careful pencil sketches of birds, each one drawn with remarkable detail.

"Wow, I love drawing birds too!" Sara said happily, leaning closer for a better look. She offered to share her own sketchbook, which was full of similar drawings.

Lama's expression changed completely, and she finally smiled for the first time that day. She explained quietly that her grandfather had taught her to sketch birds back in her old city, and that drawing them now made her feel a little less far from home.

The awkwardness melted away as the two girls spent the rest of recess talking eagerly about their favorite birds to sketch. After that day, Lama was never alone again. She sat with Sara at lunch every single day, and the two of them sketched together at every recess, trading tips and comparing drawings. Slowly but surely, a quiet new classmate had become a true, close friend.

versions.title: The Quiet New Friend
versions.text:
Sara was a conscientious, remarkably attentive student in Grade 5 at a school in Riyadh. That particular academic year, a reticent new girl named Lama had joined her class, having relocated from another city and consequently leaving behind every friend she had ever known throughout her previous schooling.

Every single day, without exception, Lama sat by herself. She consumed her lunch alone, and she spent recess alone as well, as though she had become entirely imperceptible within the busy, noisy schoolyard surrounding her. None of her classmates seemed to perceive her presence, or if they occasionally did notice, nobody made any genuine effort whatsoever to incorporate her into their games or their conversations.

Sara, however, did notice, and the observation gradually weighed upon her conscience with increasing persistence. Day after day, watching Lama sit by herself began to trouble her considerably, and she often contemplated, with a steadily growing sense of empathy, what it must feel like to be perpetually surrounded by people yet remain entirely alone, unnoticed within an otherwise familiar crowd. At first she articulated nothing, uncertain of precisely what to do, but gradually she began to experience genuine sympathy for the reticent new classmate. One afternoon, having finally summoned sufficient courage to act instead of merely observing from a comfortable distance, Sara proceeded across the yard and situated herself beside her.

"Hi, I'm Sara," she said, extending a small, friendly smile. "Can I sit here with you?"

Lama glanced upward slowly, visibly hesitant and clearly astonished that anyone wanted to sit beside her, before managing only a quiet "okay." Clutched in her hands was a notebook, filled with meticulous pencil sketches of birds, each one rendered with a remarkable, patient precision that strongly suggested countless hours of dedicated practice.

"Wow, I love drawing birds too!" Sara exclaimed happily, leaning closer for a better examination. She offered to share her own sketchbook, a seemingly minor gesture that nonetheless appeared to mean a considerable deal to a girl who had received so little attention recently.

Lama's expression transformed entirely, and she finally smiled for the first time that entire day. She explained quietly that her grandfather had instructed her in sketching birds back in her previous city, and that drawing them now, in this unfamiliar environment, made her feel marginally less distant from home.

The initial awkwardness dissipated almost immediately as the two girls devoted the remainder of recess to conversing enthusiastically about their favorite birds to sketch, comparing techniques and admiring each other's careful work. Subsequently, Lama was never alone again, sitting with Sara at lunch every single day and sketching alongside her at every recess, exchanging techniques and comparing drawings.

Sara often reflected afterward that such a small, seemingly inconsequential decision, merely walking over and extending a greeting, had fundamentally transformed another person's day, and quite possibly her entire academic year. By offering genuine companionship to one reticent classmate, Sara had, without even realizing it at the time, acquired one of her own closest and most loyal friends, while simultaneously gaining an enduring perspective on how profoundly a single, small act of kindness can ultimately matter to someone who feels entirely overlooked.

questions.stem: What is this story mostly about?

A girl who notices a classmate sitting alone and becomes her friend
A girl who moves to a new school and gets lost
A girl who teaches her whole class about many different kinds of colorful birds

wrong.C: Lama is the one who moved; nobody gets lost.

MID.prompt: Explain why Sara's small action made such a big difference to Lama. Use at least two details from the story.

MID.modelAnswer: Sara's small action mattered because Lama had been completely alone since moving to a new school. When Sara walked over and sat with her, Lama finally had someone to talk to. questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the story?

questions.stem: Based on the story, why might Sara's gesture of sharing her sketchbook matter so much to Lama?

To give Lama's hobby a deeper, personal meaning connected to home

wrong.B: The story does not claim only grandparents can teach art.

HIGH.prompt: Do you agree that a single small act of kindness can truly change someone's day, or even their whole year? Support your argument with evidence from the story, and address a counterargument.
checklist: I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that a single small act of kindness can change someone's year. Before Sara sat down, Lama had been completely alone since moving schools, with no one making the effort to include her. Sharing a sketchbook seems tiny, but it gave Lama real companionship and let her feel connected to home through her grandfather's hobby. Someone might argue that one conversation cannot fix real loneliness, but the story shows that it was exactly this small gesture that opened the door to a lasting, close friendship.
